messages:
marie: FYI — onboarding Pages sample started failing after the recent exports refactor. Deploy-time error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'RetryPolicy').

oliver: Can you paste the package.json exports that the sample pulled in?

marie: Snippet from the template we shipped:
```json
"exports": {
  "./*": "./dist/*",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
No explicit top-level `.` mapping and no `types` top-level field.

sophie: That wildcard makes the bundler pick the ESM .mjs entry which, after the rollup change, is a default-only wrapper. Our old CJS build had named exports so local ts-node tests passed. Pages is ESM-only, so it hits the default and named symbols are missing.

oliver: So both runtime and editor fail: runtime can't find named export, and tsserver auto-imports point at dist/index.mjs and complains about missing declarations.

marie: Repro: in a clean ESM project `import sdk from 'redwood-sdk'; console.log(sdk.RetryPolicy)` -> undefined.

ryan: Proposed quick fixes:
1) Add explicit top-level "." export with conditional `import`/`require` pointing to `dist/index.mjs` and `dist/index.cjs`.
2) Add top-level "types": "dist/index.d.ts" so editors resolve declarations.
3) Make rollup emit named re-exports rather than a default wrapper (we used to do a small interop shim).

marie: Workaround for now patched into the sample: `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'; const { RetryPolicy } = Redwood.default ?? Redwood;` ugly but unblocks Pages. Documented in onboarding notes.

ci-bot: created issue #4467 and draft PR by ryan: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1402 — PR adds `."` conditional export, top-level types field, and restores named-exports interop in the ESM bundle.

oliver: Long-term: add CI smoke test that installs the built package into a pure-ESM sandbox (Cloudflare Pages emulator / Bun / Deno) and runs `tsc --noEmit` against samples to catch missing types. Also add a lint rule to flag `require()` usage in sample repos.

sophie: Agree. Also add a tiny integration that runs the onboarding template in a container with node >=16 --input-type=module to catch default/named mismatches.

marie: I've informed onboarding and CS about the temporary workaround and which customers might be affected. Marking this thread as tracked until PR merges. :thumbsup:
